newsitem.title: FINLAND: Raisio says Benecol to keep high value.
newsitem.headline: Raisio says Benecol to keep high value.

text.p: Finnish foods, animal feeds and chemicals group Raision Tehtaat Oy said on Thursday products carrying its cholesterol-reducing Benecol agent will remain expensive due to the high costs of key ingredient, plant sterol.

"The price of margarine will not fall as the price of plant sterol -- regardless of how it is processed -- will always have quite a high price," Raisio CEO Matti Salminen told reporters after the group held a briefing on the agent.
The key plant sterol ingredient makes about half the costs of the active agent, he said, but declined to give figures.
Benecol margarine's retail price is about 100 markka per kilo in Finland, which is for the time being the only market where the product is sold.
Margarines without the Benecol active agent cost about 20 markka per kilo.
Salminen said, consequently, Benecol products will only be sold in the countries with sufficient purchasing power.
He named North America and Japan as potential areas in addition to northern and central Europe.
Plant sterol has been proven to reduce cholesterol and Raisio's invention is to adapt the molecule to make it fat-soluble -- a stanol ester.

But Raisio vice president Kari Jokinen said processing costs of plant sterol in Raisio's second stanol ester factory, to be completed by the end of 1997, will be clearly lower than in the first plant, due to come on stream at the end of 1996.
"The costs per kilo produced will be clearly cheaper," he said.
Raisio said earlier its esterification capacity is expected to rise to 2,000 tonnes per year by 2000.
